# Harkness Training Solutions

> Harkness Training Solutions (HTS) helps leaders, especially new managers, rehearse hard conversations before they are real. Mishandled conversations cost teams trust, talent, and time.

Harkness Training Solutions trains leaders and teams to handle high-stakes conversations under pressure. A session has three parts. Learn a simple storytelling framework: character, goal, challenge, resolution. Practice the conversation you are actually dreading with an improv actor briefed to push back the way the other person would: interrupting, doubting, going quiet. Feedback from peers, immediately, in the form “When you said ___, I felt ___.” Then you run it again.

This is for leaders, especially new managers. Many of them work at hard-tech companies in the South Bay of Los Angeles: space, defense, and aerospace. It is not only for engineers. An individual can start at a free Open Lab and can join the monthly Practice Lab. A team starts with a free 20-minute demo or a Kickoff, then a Pilot or the Full Program.

Sessions run online and in person. Every Open Lab has an online session at noon Pacific. Once a month there is also an in-person session in El Segundo at 6 PM Pacific. Team sessions run online, at your site, or in El Segundo. The address on the site is 222 N. Pacific Coast Hwy, El Segundo, CA. In-person room details go out after registration. Keep scenarios general and unclassified: no names, program names, customers, or export-controlled details. Sessions are recorded so you can see where the conversation turned.

Contact: hello@harknesstraining.com, (310) 896-5379.

Company accounts only: LinkedIn https://www.linkedin.com/company/144037123, YouTube https://www.youtube.com/@harknesstraining, X https://x.com/harknesstrainin (@harknesstrainin), Instagram https://www.instagram.com/harknesstraining (@harknesstraining).

## What a mishandled conversation costs

Trust, talent, and time. It costs the person who has the conversation and the team around them. On the site, that shows up as stalled decisions, bad news that arrives too late, a risk hidden until it is late, rework, and a good engineer who leaves. The site does not publish a dollar figure for that cost.

Prices below are the public list prices, per person. Founding rates lock in for teams that start by Dec 31, 2026. Teams of 15 to 20 people get 10% off the Kickoff, Pilot, and Full Program. Over 20 people, ask for a cohort quote. The team rate does not apply to Practice Lab.

- Custom programs: quoted. Tell us the conversations your leaders keep facing. HTS writes the scenarios, briefs actors to push back the way your people do, and runs it on your schedule. https://harknesstraining.com/custom

## FAQ

Is this for me, or for my team?
Both. A mishandled conversation costs the person who has it and the team around them. Individual leaders start at a free Open Lab and can join the monthly Practice Lab. Teams start with a free 20-minute demo or a Kickoff, then a Pilot or the Full Program.

Do I need a conversation ready?
It helps. Bring the one you keep putting off: that's usually the one most likely to go wrong. Keep it general, with no names, programs or customers. If you'd rather watch, tick “I'd rather watch this time” when you save a seat.

Why would an engineer need this?
At a certain level, the job is mostly conversations. A mishandled one can sink a good design, hide a risk until it's late, or cost you a good engineer. You were promoted for your technical judgment. Nobody trained you for the conversation where you have to defend it.

What happens at an Open Lab?
We start with why conversations get mishandled, then spend 5 to 10 minutes on a simple storytelling framework. Then the hot seat: one person runs a conversation they're dreading with an improv actor, the room gives feedback (“When you said ___, I felt ___”), and they run it again with the feedback.

Who are the actors?
Improv actors, briefed to push back the way the other person would: interrupting, doubting, going quiet. Pressure is where conversations get mishandled, so that's where we practice.

Why practice with peers watching?
Most mishandled conversations go uncorrected because nobody tells you how your words landed. Here, everyone does. Each observer writes a 4×6 card: “When you said ___, I felt ___.” Then you go again.

Is it recorded? What about sensitive work?
Sessions are recorded so you can see exactly where a conversation turned. Keep scenarios general and unclassified: no program names, customers or export-controlled details.

Online or in person? What time?
Both, because hard conversations happen on video and across the table. Every Open Lab has an online session at noon Pacific. Once a month there's also an in-person session in El Segundo at 6 PM Pacific. Team sessions run online, at your site, or in El Segundo.

How can new managers practice difficult conversations?
Bring the conversation you keep putting off to a free Open Lab, or practice it with your team in a Kickoff, Pilot, or the Full Program. A session is the same shape either way. You spend 5 to 10 minutes on a simple storytelling framework, then one person runs the conversation with an improv actor who pushes back. Peers say how it landed (“When you said ___, I felt ___”), and you run it again. If you'd rather watch, you can.

What does a mishandled conversation cost a team?
Trust, talent, and time. It costs the person who has it and the team around them. A mishandled conversation can stall a decision, hide a risk until it's late, or cost the team a good engineer.

What is an Open Lab?
Open Lab is free and runs 90 minutes. It starts with why conversations get mishandled, then 5 to 10 minutes on a storytelling framework: character, goal, challenge, resolution. One person practices a conversation they are dreading with an improv actor, the room gives feedback, and they run it again. Upcoming online sessions are 12:00–1:30 PM Pacific on Thursday, November 19, 2026; Thursday, December 10, 2026; and Thursday, January 7, 2027. December 10 also has an in-person session in El Segundo at 6:00–7:30 PM Pacific.

Who is Harkness Training for?
Leaders who have hard conversations to handle, especially new managers. Many of them work at hard-tech companies in the South Bay: space, defense, and aerospace. An individual can start at a free Open Lab. A team can start with a free 20-minute demo or a Kickoff.
